privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What this site collects, what for, and how long it is kept.
paragraphs: The short version: you do not need to give us anything to read this site. If you create an account, we keep your email and, if there are any, a name to show and a photo of you that is not published. If you sign up to bring a good, we keep the contact name and a phone number or an email. If you leave only a phone number, with no account, we keep your name and that number so we can call you, and the item stays reserved in your name until the person who coordinates confirms. We do not use third-party cookies and we do not follow you across other pages.

sections.heading: What we do not do
paragraphs: You do not need an account to browse the site, and browsing asks for nothing. There is no newsletter. Covering an item with money does not ask for an account or a phone: the transfer is the proof. Signing up to bring a good asks for a name and a phone number or an email. With the email an account is created. With the phone number, with no account, the item is reserved in your name until the person who coordinates confirms.
Payments are not processed on the site: you make the transfer from your bank, and that operation is between your bank and ours.
We do not use advertising cookies, social-media pixels or services that build a profile of you.

sections.heading: If you create an account
paragraphs: Creating an account is optional and serves one purpose: to be able to say "I am bringing this one" and have it written down as yours, so you can see it and cancel it. Confirming the email is not proof that the donation is real: it is so we can write to you.

From you we keep your email, the language you prefer to be written in, and a name and a photo if there are any: you write them, or the network you signed in with brings them if those fields were still empty here. Your password is not kept: what is kept is an encrypted result that cannot be turned back into your password. If that address already had an account, signing in with Google (or another network) uses that one: a second account is not created.
The name shown is the one you choose —or the one the network suggests, which you can change. It is never derived from your email. If there is none, there is none.

The photo, if you upload one or if the network brought one, identifies you while you are signed in. It is not published on any page of the site, it does not appear in Who helped, and it is not shared.
Your email is not published on any page, is not shared with anyone, and is not used to send you anything other than messages about your account or about something you offered to bring.

The service that runs the accounts also records when you sign in, with the IP address and the browser you sign in from. It is there to detect attempts to get into other people's accounts. The family does not use that information for anything else.

If the site offers signing in with a network (Google, for example), that network learns that you used this site: that is the trade-off of signing in without inventing a password. We receive your email, and if you did not already have a name or photo here, we copy those from that network into your profile. They are not published: the wall stays anonymous until you choose to appear, and the photo does not leave the site.
Your account is kept until you delete it. You can delete it yourself from your account, without asking us and without giving reasons: your email, your name and your photo are deleted right away.

sections.heading: What is measured
paragraphs: We count visits and a few use events: how many people come, from what kind of link they arrive, how many times a bank detail is copied, how many times the page is shared and from which country it is opened.
Those measurements are aggregated and cannot be tied to a person. We do not keep your full IP address, or an identifier that follows you between visits.
They serve one thing: to know whether the page is understood and whether the path to help works.

sections.heading: Gifts
paragraphs: If you give by transfer, your bank tells ours the details of the operation. That information stays in the internal accounting record and is used to reconcile the totals.
The name of the person who gave and the individual amount are not published.
The internal record is kept while the campaign is open and for as long as the accounting requires.

sections.heading: Expense receipts
paragraphs: Invoices and receipts for the work are stored in private storage. They are not public because they often hold third-party data, such as a supplier's name and address.
The file can be reviewed by a person with an auditor role, with a temporary access.

sections.heading: If you offer to bring something
paragraphs: Signing up to bring a material stores, besides your email if you opened an account, your contact name and a phone number if you leave one, how much you committed to bring and until when that hold is good. The item page does not ask for a pickup address. None of that is published. How you appear is chosen in your account.

If you leave a phone number without creating an account, we keep your name and that number, and the item stays reserved. The number is not published. The contact name is not either: it is not the name on the wall. If the person who coordinates confirms they got in touch and you agreed to appear, that screen is where the display name and, if you want, a private note are recorded. If they do not confirm, the hold is released.

The name you want shown, on the account path, is optional, and the default is not to appear. It is chosen in your account, not when you sign up. If you write it and uncheck that you prefer not to appear, it is published on Who helped only when the material arrives.
If you delete the account, your email, your name, your photo, your phone and the pickup address are deleted. Holds that were already fulfilled stay as a fact about the work, without identifying you.

The emails we send you are about your account or a hold of yours: that we received it, that it was written down, that expiry is near, that it arrived, or that it was cancelled. There is no list and no broadcast.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
paragraphs: If this policy changes, the date in the heading changes and the change is recorded in the public history of the site's code.
For questions about this policy, the published email is justomiguelvargas@gmail.com.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: What this site is, what it is not, and what you can expect from it.
paragraphs: This site belongs to Norma's family and exists to raise the funds to rebuild their house and to account for how they are used.

sections.heading: What a gift is
paragraphs: A gift is a voluntary donation to a family. It is not a purchase, it does not entitle you to anything in return, and it is not tax-deductible: the project is not an entity with legal personality.
Gifts are not returned, except for a transfer error that can be shown with the bank receipt.

sections.heading: What the money is used for
paragraphs: On the work on the house: materials, labour, services, tools and transport. Each expense is published on the transparency page with its date, its description, its category and what share of total spending it is. Amounts are not published: 100% of the work is not closed yet.
If money is ever left over from the work, the destination will be published before it is used.

sections.heading: Accuracy of the information
paragraphs: The published figures are updated after reconciliation with the bank, so they may be a few days behind reality. The date of the last reconciliation is always visible.
When a fact has not yet been verified, the section is omitted. This site does not show sample amounts, dates or bank details.

sections.heading: Beware of fake sites
paragraphs: Always check the address of the site before you transfer. If the bank details you see do not match the ones we share on our channels, do not transfer.
We will never ask you for a password, a code from your bank or your card details.

sections.heading: Content
paragraphs: The texts and photographs on the site belong to the family. They may be shared to spread the campaign; they may not be used for commercial purposes.
